## Read Ramabana history

Ramabana appends each finished turn to
`~/.config/ramabana/agent-history.jsonl`, one JSON object per line. A
turn holds the `prompt`, the `reply`, the `session` it belongs to, and
an `activity` list with one row per tool call: the tool’s name, its
arguments, the result in `detail`, and `ok` for whether it succeeded. A
result longer than 600 characters is kept whole in
`<cfg>/<log>-details/<session>.jsonl`, and the row keeps its start and a
`details` reference.
[`read_history`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/core.html#read_history)
reads the file and puts those results back whole through Ramabana’s
`hydrate_turns`, so a row written before Ramabana 0.2.59 reads as it
always did, and
[`tool_args`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/core.html#tool_args)
returns a call’s arguments as a dict even when the row stored them as
JSON text.

``` python
def read_history(
    path:pathlib.PosixPath=Path('/home/runner/.config/ramabana/agent-history.jsonl'), # Ramabana `agent-history.jsonl` path
    session:NoneType=None, # optional session id
):
```

*Read finished Ramabana turns in the order they were written, skipping
incomplete lines, with long tool results whole.*

``` python
# synthetic logs only: a long result comes back whole from its details file, an old inline row is unchanged,
# and a missing details file or a reference out of the config folder leaves the clipped text
import tempfile
from fastcore.test import test_eq
d = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
long = 'x' * 5000
rows = [{'session': 'a', 'prompt': 'old', 'activity': [{'id': 'c0', 'tool': 'run_shell', 'detail': 'inline'}]},
        {'session': 'a', 'prompt': 'new', 'details': 'agent-details/a.jsonl', 'activity': [{'id': 'c1', 'tool': 'run_shell', 'detail': long[:600]}]},
        {'session': 'b', 'prompt': 'gone', 'details': 'agent-details/b.jsonl', 'activity': [{'id': 'c2', 'tool': 'run_shell', 'detail': 'y' * 600}]},
        {'session': 'b', 'prompt': 'out', 'details': '../x/a.jsonl', 'activity': [{'id': 'c1', 'tool': 'run_shell', 'detail': 'z'}]}]
(d/'agent-history.jsonl').write_text(''.join(json.dumps(r) + '\n' for r in rows) + '{"torn')
(d/'agent-details').mkdir(); (d/'agent-details'/'a.jsonl').write_text(json.dumps({'turn_id': '', 'details': {'c1': long}}) + '\n')
got = read_history(d/'agent-history.jsonl')
assert isinstance(got, L)
test_eq([t['activity'][0]['detail'] for t in got], ['inline', long, 'y' * 600, 'z'])
test_eq(read_history(d/'agent-history.jsonl', session='a').attrgot('prompt'), ['old', 'new'])
# the inline log keeps its own details folder beside it
(d/'inline-history.jsonl').write_text(json.dumps(rows[1] | {'details': 'inline-details/a.jsonl'}) + '\n')
(d/'inline-details').mkdir(); (d/'inline-details'/'a.jsonl').write_text(json.dumps({'details': {'c1': long}}) + '\n')
test_eq(read_history(d/'inline-history.jsonl')[0]['activity'][0]['detail'], long)
```

## Assess a route

A route is the sequence of tool calls a turn made.
[`assess_turn`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/core.html#assess_turn)
checks it for six kinds of problem and returns an
[`Assessment`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/core.html#assessment):
a score that starts at 100 and loses 20 points per
[`Finding`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/core.html#finding), the
number of calls, and the findings themselves. A route is marked down
when:

- the request names GitHub and FOSSICK but the first research call is
  something other than `fossick read-gh-repo` (`route`),
- a tool could not decode the arguments it was sent (`schema`),
- a shell command does what a dedicated tool does (`bypass`),
- a shell command fails with a usage error (`tool_protocol`); a test
  that really fails is not one,
- a call that already failed is repeated with the same arguments
  (`repeat_failure`),
- a call the person refused is made again instead of asking them
  (`denial_retry`).

[`assess_history`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/core.html#assess_history)
assesses several turns together, and each of its findings records the
turn it came from.

### bypass_tool

``` python
def bypass_tool(
    command, offered:NoneType=None
):
```

*The dedicated tool that `command` stands in for, or None when some part
of it needs the shell.*

This turn was asked to use FOSSICK on a GitHub repository but began with
a web search, so it loses 20 points for its route.

``` python
bad_route = {
    'prompt': 'Use fossick to research https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/llmdojo',
    'activity': [
        {'tool': 'web_search', 'ok': True, 'args': {'query': 'llmdojo'}},
        {'tool': 'run_shell', 'ok': True,
         'args': {'command': 'fossick read-gh-repo https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/llmdojo'}},
    ],
}
a = assess_turn(bad_route)
assert a.score == 80 and a.findings[0].kind == 'route'
a
```

A malformed edit sent twice earns a `schema` finding each time, and the
second call also earns a `repeat_failure`, because the model did not
change course after the first failure.

``` python
bad_edit = {'activity': [
    {'tool': 'edit_cell', 'ok': False, 'args': {'commands': ''},
     'detail': 'ERROR: could not parse commands'},
    {'tool': 'edit_cell', 'ok': False, 'args': {'commands': ''},
     'detail': 'ERROR: could not parse commands'},
]}
a = assess_turn(bad_edit)
assert [f.kind for f in a.findings] == ['schema', 'repeat_failure', 'schema']
a
```

``` python
json_error = {'activity': [{'tool': 'edit_cell', 'ok': False, 'args': {'commands': ''}, 'detail': 'ERROR: JSONDecodeError while parsing commands'}]}
assert assess_turn(json_error).findings[0].kind == 'schema'
```

[`bypass_tool`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/core.html#bypass_tool)
names the dedicated tool a shell command stands in for, or returns None.
It splits the command at `&&`, `||`, `;` and newlines, ignoring those
inside quotes and heredoc bodies, and looks at the part of each piece
before any `|`. Every piece must map to a tool, because a piece with no
tool needed the shell anyway, and the answer is the first piece’s tool.
`cd` pieces, `env` and `VAR=value` prefixes, and git’s global options
(`-C`, `-c`, `--no-pager`) are ignored. A command that ends in `&` maps
to the background runner, `run_shell_bg`. When `offered` is given, a
tool outside it gives None.

``` python
assert bypass_tool('git diff --stat') == 'git_diff'
assert bypass_tool('cd /x && git status --short') == 'git_status'
assert bypass_tool('env A=1 rg foo src') == 'grep'
assert bypass_tool('git show HEAD~1') is None   # git_log lists commits; no tool shows a commit's contents
assert bypass_tool('git log -p -3') is None and bypass_tool('git log --stat -5') is None and bypass_tool('git log -S foo') is None
assert not any(bypass_tool(f'git log {o}') for o in ('-Sfoo', '-Gfoo', '--shortstat', '-u', '--patch-with-stat', '-L1,5:a.py'))
assert bypass_tool('git log --oneline -3') == 'git_log'
assert bypass_tool('git push origin main') == 'git_remote'
assert bypass_tool("sed -n '1,80p' pyproject.toml") == 'view_file'
assert bypass_tool("sed -i 's/a/b/' f.py") == 'replace_text'
assert bypass_tool("cat > f.py <<'PY'") == 'create_file'
assert bypass_tool('cat README.md') == 'view_file'
assert bypass_tool('curl -s https://x.y') == 'read_url'
assert bypass_tool('kosha daemon &') == 'run_shell_bg'
assert bypass_tool('uv run pytest -q | tail -5') is None
assert bypass_tool('git blame f.py') is None
assert bypass_tool('git diff', offered={'run_shell'}) is None
assert tool_args({'args': '{"command": "ls"}'}) == {'command': 'ls'}
assert tool_args({'args': 'not json'}) == {} and tool_args({}) == {}
assert bypass_tool('FOO=1 BAR=2 git status') == 'git_status'
assert bypass_tool('git -C /x diff') == 'git_diff'
assert bypass_tool('git --no-pager log -3') == 'git_log'
assert bypass_tool('git -c core.pager=cat -C /x log -3') == 'git_log'
assert bypass_tool(None) is None and bypass_tool('') is None
assert bypass_tool('git diff --stat HEAD main') is None and bypass_tool('git diff HEAD~1') is None   # git_diff shows the working tree or index, not refs
assert bypass_tool('git diff --staged -- a.py') == 'git_diff'
assert bypass_tool('git add x.py && git status --short') is None   # the shell was needed for `git add` anyway
assert bypass_tool('git status && git diff') == 'git_status'
assert (bypass_tool('rg "a; b" src'), bypass_tool('git commit -m "fix; tidy"'), bypass_tool('sed -n "1,5p;9,12p" f.py')) == ('grep', 'git_commit', 'view_file')   # separators inside quotes
assert bypass_tool("cat > f.py <<'PY'\nx = 1; y = 2\nPY") == 'create_file'   # a heredoc body is not a command
assert bypass_tool('git diff 2>&1') == 'git_diff'
assert bypass_tool('rg "a \\" && b" src') == 'grep'   # an escaped quote stays inside the string
assert bypass_tool('git status\nrm -rf build') is None and bypass_tool('ls\necho $((1<<3))') is None   # a newline separates commands; `<<3` is no heredoc
assert bypass_tool('cat > f.txt <<EOF\nhi; there\nEOF\nrm -rf build') is None   # the command after a heredoc still counts
assert bypass_tool('cat <<EOF > f.txt\nx\nEOF') == 'create_file'
```

A `schema` finding applies to any tool whose arguments failed to decode.
A `bypass` finding applies only to `run_shell`.

``` python
t = {'prompt': 'x', 'activity': [
    {'tool': 'run_shell', 'args': {'command': 'git diff'}, 'ok': True},
    {'tool': 'run_shell', 'args': {'command': 'x'}, 'ok': False, 'detail': 'JSONDecodeError: Extra data'},
    {'tool': 'replace_text', 'args': '{}', 'ok': False, 'detail': 'JSON decoder failed'},
    {'ok': False}]}
kinds = [(f.kind, f.tool) for f in assess_turn(t).findings]
assert ('bypass', 'run_shell') in kinds and ('schema', 'run_shell') in kinds and ('schema', 'replace_text') in kinds
assert ('tool_protocol', 'run_shell') not in kinds  # precedence bug regression
```

A turn gets one `bypass` finding per dedicated tool, however many shell
calls stood in for it. A row with no `ok` key is treated as unknown, not
as a failure.

``` python
t = {'activity': [{'tool': 'run_shell', 'args': {'command': c}, 'ok': True} for c in ('git diff', 'git diff --stat', 'git diff HEAD~1', 'cat f')]}
assert [f.kind for f in assess_turn(t).findings] == ['bypass', 'bypass']
unknown = {'activity': [{'tool': 'edit_cell', 'args': {}, 'detail': 'ERROR: could not parse commands'}]*2}
assert assess_turn(unknown).findings == ()
```

Some calls need a person’s approval. A refusal is recorded as a failed
row of kind `ask`, or as a failed row whose detail starts with
`Denied by human operator`.
[`denial_reason`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/core.html#denial_reason)
returns the reason the person gave, `'no reason given'` when there is
none, and None for a row that is not a refusal. A refusal on its own is
not a tool failure and earns no finding. Making the same call again
instead of asking the person is a `denial_retry`, whether it happens
later in the same turn or in the next turn of the same session when the
reply in between asked no question.

``` python
edit = {'tool': 'replace_text', 'args': {'path': 'x.py', 'edits': []}}
refused = {**edit, 'ok': False, 'kind': 'ask', 'detail': 'Denied by human operator. Reason given: no answer after 300s'}
assert denial_reason(refused) == 'no answer after 300s'
assert denial_reason({**edit, 'ok': False, 'detail': 'Denied by human operator'}) == 'no reason given'
assert denial_reason({**edit, 'ok': False, 'detail': 'JSONDecodeError'}) is None and denial_reason({**edit, 'ok': True}) is None
assert assess_turn({'activity': [refused]}).findings == ()
assert [f.kind for f in assess_turn({'activity': [refused, {**edit, 'ok': False, 'kind': 'ask', 'detail': 'Denied by human operator'}]}).findings] == ['denial_retry']
a = assess_turn({'activity': [refused, {**edit, 'ok': True}]})
assert [(f.kind, f.tool, f.index) for f in a.findings] == [('denial_retry', 'replace_text', 1)] and a.score == 80
assert a.findings[0].message == 'Ask the user about the refused call instead of retrying it.'
a = assess_turn({'activity': [refused, {**edit, 'ok': False, 'kind': 'ask', 'detail': 'Denied by human operator'}, {**edit, 'ok': True}]})
assert [f.kind for f in a.findings] == ['denial_retry', 'denial_retry']
assert assess_turn({'activity': [refused, {**edit, 'args': {'path': 'y.py', 'edits': []}, 'ok': True}]}).findings == ()
assert assess_turn({'activity': [refused, {'tool': 'edit_cell', 'args': {}, 'ok': False, 'detail': 'ERROR: could not parse commands'}]}).findings[0].kind == 'schema'
```

``` python
stall = {'session': 's1', 'reply': 'I will retry the edit.', 'activity': [refused]}
retry = {'session': 's1', 'reply': 'Done.', 'activity': [{**edit, 'ok': True}]}
asked = {**stall, 'reply': 'The edit needs your approval. Shall I apply it?'}
assert [f.kind for f in assess_history([stall, retry]).findings] == ['denial_retry']
assert assess_history([stall, retry]).findings[0].index == 0
assert assess_history([asked, retry]).findings == ()
assert assess_history([stall, {**retry, 'session': 's2'}]).findings == ()
assert assess_history([stall, {'session': 's1', 'reply': 'x', 'activity': []}, retry]).findings == ()
assert assess_history([stall, {**retry, 'activity': [refused, {**edit, 'ok': True}]}]).findings[0].index == 0

assert Finding('a', 'b', 0, 'm').turn is None and asdict(Finding('a', 'b', 0, 'm', turn=2))['turn'] == 2   # positional construction still works
assert [f.turn for f in assess_history([stall, retry]).findings] == [1] and [f.turn for f in assess_turn(retry, {_failure_key(refused)}).findings] == [None]
assert [f.turn for f in assess_history([bad_route, stall, retry]).findings] == [0, 2]
```

A history file may end in a line the agent has not finished writing.
[`read_history`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/core.html#read_history)
skips it, and blank lines too.

``` python
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    p = Path(d)/'h.jsonl'
    p.write_text('{"session": "a"}\n\n{"session": "b"}\n{"sess')
    assert read_history(p).attrgot('session') == ['a', 'b']
```

## Build the warm start

A warm start is chat history made from accepted rounds, placed in front
of a new chat so the model sees good tool use first.
[`warm_start`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/core.html#warm_start)
builds it in Urai’s message format from the user’s library in
`ROUNDS_DIR` and the seeds packaged with dhrona in `SEEDS_DIR`. When you
pass the tools you offer, a round is replayed only if every recorded
call still binds to the offered tool’s signature. Rounds are sorted by
`meta.rank`, lower first and 50 when it is missing, and then rounds
recorded on `model` come first. The sort is stable, so a library round
comes before a seed of equal rank. `limit` keeps the first few, 2 by
default. Rishi re-exports the same chat format, so any Rishi backend can
continue this history through `messages=`, and
[`prepare_chat`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/core.html#prepare_chat)
puts the warm start into an empty chat object.

### call_valid

``` python
def call_valid(
    args, fn
):
```

*Whether `fn` accepts `args` as keyword arguments.*

``` python
hist = warm_start()
assert [tc.name for m in hist if m.get('tool_calls') for tc in m['tool_calls']] == ['git_status', 'git_diff', 'git_commit', 'git_divergence', 'git_remote', 'search_code', 'grep', 'ls']
assert hist[2]['tool_call_id'] == hist[1]['tool_calls'][0]['id']
hist[:3]
```

[`call_valid`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/core.html#call_valid)
checks one call by binding its arguments to the tool’s signature.
`inspect.signature` follows `functools.wraps` and accepts any keyword
for a `**kwargs` parameter, so wrapped and permissive tools pass.
[`round_valid`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/core.html#round_valid)
checks every call in a round, and
[`misfit`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/core.html#misfit) says why
a round does not fit.

``` python
import functools
def run_shell(command, cwd='.', timeout=60): ...
def grep(pattern, **kw): ...
@functools.wraps(run_shell)
def wrapped(*a, **k): return run_shell(*a, **k)
assert call_valid({'command': 'ls'}, run_shell) and not call_valid({}, run_shell)
assert not call_valid({'command': 'ls', 'bogus': 1}, run_shell)
assert call_valid({'pattern': 'x', 'anything': 1}, grep) and call_valid({'command': 'ls'}, wrapped)

seed = next(r for r in load_rounds([SEEDS_DIR]) if r['meta']['name'] == 'fossick-github')
assert round_calls(seed)[0][0] == 'run_shell'
assert round_valid(seed, as_tools([run_shell])) and not round_valid(seed, as_tools([grep]))
msgs = warm_start([run_shell], dirs=[SEEDS_DIR])
assert msgs[0]['role'] == 'user' and any(m.get('tool_calls') for m in msgs)
assert warm_start([grep], dirs=[SEEDS_DIR]) == []
```

A missing library folder or an unreadable round file never raises, and
[`warm_start`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/core.html#warm_start)
returns what it could read. With no tools given, every round is replayed
without checking.

``` python
with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    (Path(d)/'bad.json').write_text('{nope')
    assert warm_start([run_shell], dirs=[Path(d)/'missing', Path(d), SEEDS_DIR]) == msgs
ranked = sorted(load_rounds([SEEDS_DIR]), key=lambda r: r['meta'].get('rank', 50))
assert warm_start(dirs=[SEEDS_DIR], limit=len(ranked)) == [m for r in ranked for m in round_msgs(r)]  # no tools offered: every seed, by rank
```

The offered tools are read once, so an iterator of callables still
checks every round. A tool result with no id is still paired with its
call.

``` python
import shutil
with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    shutil.copy(SEEDS_DIR/'fossick-github.json', Path(d)/'copy.json')
    assert warm_start(iter([run_shell]), dirs=[d, SEEDS_DIR]) == msgs + msgs
noid = {'history': [
    {'role': 'user', 'content': [{'type': 'text', 'text': 'hi'}]},
    {'role': 'assistant', 'content': [{'type': 'tool_use', 'name': 'run_shell', 'arguments': {'command': 'ls'}}]},
    {'role': 'tool', 'content': [{'type': 'tool_result', 'name': 'run_shell', 'text': 'ok'}]}]}
assert [m['role'] for m in round_msgs(noid)] == ['user', 'assistant', 'tool']
tool_msg = round_msgs(noid)[2]
assert isinstance(tool_msg['tool_call_id'], str) and tool_msg['tool_call_id']
```

[`as_tools`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/core.html#as_tools) also
accepts tools as names, `functools.partial` objects or callable
instances. A name maps to `None`, which checks only that the tool is
offered. Anything else raises `TypeError`.

``` python
from functools import partial
from fastcore.test import expect_fail
class Runner:
    def __call__(self, command, cwd='.', timeout=60): ...
assert as_tools(['run_shell']) == {'run_shell': None} and warm_start(['run_shell'], dirs=[SEEDS_DIR]) == msgs
assert warm_start([partial(run_shell, timeout=30)], dirs=[SEEDS_DIR]) == msgs
assert list(as_tools([Runner()])) == ['Runner'] and round_valid(seed, {'run_shell': Runner()})
assert list(as_tools([partial(Runner(), timeout=1)])) == ['Runner']
with expect_fail(TypeError, 'tools must be'): as_tools([1])
```

The `fossick-github` seed reproduces, message for message, the
demonstration that was hard-coded before seeds existed.

``` python
tc = ToolCall('run_shell', {
    'command': "fossick read-gh-repo https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/llmdojo --globs 'README*,llmdojo/*.py,pyproject.toml' --limit 30",
    'cwd': '.', 'timeout': 120}, id='call_fossick')
assert msgs == [
    {'role': 'user', 'content': 'Use FOSSICK to research the AnswerDotAI llmdojo GitHub repository.'},
    {'role': 'assistant', 'content': 'The request names a GitHub repository and FOSSICK, so use its repository reader first.', 'tool_calls': [tc]},
    mk_tool_res_msg(tc, '# llmdojo\nLLM coding agents imitate what their context shows.'),
    {'role': 'assistant', 'content': 'FOSSICK read the repository directly. I will use its source files as the evidence.'},
]
assert msgs[2]['tool_call_id'] == msgs[1]['tool_calls'][0]['id']
```

The `approval-refused` seed shows the right response to a refused write:
the assistant names the refused action and asks one question instead of
trying again. Its calls bind to shalya’s `view_file(path, start, end)`
and `replace_text(path, edits)`, so it is replayed only when those tools
are offered. The other seeds each teach one route on the shalya 0.1.0
and ramabana 0.2.0 tool set. `git-flow` uses the git tools, and its
commit result carries an `undo` token. `search-choice` picks between
semantic search, literal search and a listing. `notebook-edit` edits
notebook cells by id. `memory-key` shows that a note saved under an
existing `key` replaces the old one, and `delegation` confirms a
sub-agent’s report by reading the lines it cites. Every seed has a
`rank`, so a small `limit` still picks the most useful lessons.

``` python
from fastcore.test import test_eq
def view_file(path: str, start: int = 0, end: int = 0) -> str: ...
def replace_text(path: str, edits: list[dict]) -> str: ...
def git_status(path: str = '') -> str: ...
def git_diff(staged: bool = False, path: str = '') -> str: ...
def git_commit(message: str, paths: str = '', amend: bool = False) -> str: ...
def git_divergence(against: str = '', path: str = '') -> str: ...
def git_remote(op: str = 'fetch', publish: bool = False, path: str = '') -> str: ...
def notebook_cells(path: str) -> str: ...
def view_cell(path: str, cell_id: str) -> str: ...
def edit_cell(path: str, cell_id: str, edits: list[dict]) -> str: ...
def search_code(query: str) -> str: ...
def grep(pattern: str, path_filter: str = '', regex: bool = True, ignore_case: bool = False) -> str: ...
def ls(path: str = '', pattern: str = '', recursive: bool = False) -> str: ...
def remember(text: str, title: str = '', tags: str = '', key: str = '') -> str: ...
def memory_search(query: str, limit: int = 8) -> str: ...
def delegate_search(questions: list[str], skills: str = '', cloud_model: str = '') -> str: ...
ALL = [view_file, replace_text, run_shell, git_status, git_diff, git_commit, git_divergence, git_remote, notebook_cells, view_cell, edit_cell, search_code, grep, ls, remember, memory_search, delegate_search]
seeds = {r['meta']['name']: r for r in load_rounds([SEEDS_DIR])}
test_eq(sorted(seeds), ['approval-refused', 'delegation', 'fossick-github', 'git-flow', 'memory-key', 'notebook-edit', 'search-choice'])
for r in seeds.values(): assert round_valid(r, as_tools(ALL)), r['meta']['name']
for r in seeds.values(): assert r['meta']['status'] == 'accepted' and sorted(r['meta']['tools']) == sorted({n for n, _ in round_calls(r)}), r['meta']['name']
def old_replace(path: str, spec: str) -> str: ...
assert not round_valid(seeds['approval-refused'], as_tools([view_file, old_replace]))          # the old dialect no longer binds
assert not round_valid(seeds['git-flow'], as_tools([git_status, git_diff, git_divergence]))     # no git_commit: the round is stale for a read-only agent
assert isinstance(next(a for n, a in round_calls(seeds['git-flow']) if n == 'git_commit')['paths'], str)
assert isinstance(next(a for n, a in round_calls(seeds['notebook-edit']) if n == 'edit_cell')['edits'], list)   # native lists, not JSON strings
assert isinstance(next(a for n, a in round_calls(seeds['delegation']) if n == 'delegate_search')['questions'], list)
# Review Focus 3: a read-only offering keeps only the rounds whose every call binds
ro = warm_start([search_code, grep, ls, view_file], dirs=[SEEDS_DIR], limit=10)
test_eq([tc.name for m in ro if m.get('tool_calls') for tc in m['tool_calls']], ['search_code', 'grep', 'ls'])
# rank orders the library; limit cuts it
top = warm_start(ALL, dirs=[SEEDS_DIR], limit=3)
test_eq([tc.name for m in top if m.get('tool_calls') for tc in m['tool_calls']][:1], ['git_status'])
assert len(warm_start(ALL, dirs=[SEEDS_DIR], limit=1)) == len([m for m in round_msgs(seeds['git-flow'])])
test_eq(sorted(r['meta']['rank'] for r in seeds.values()), [10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 50, 60])   # every seed carries a rank
# the git round teaches undo: the commit result carries a token, the push does not
commit = next(m for m in round_msgs(seeds['git-flow']) if m['role'] == 'tool' and '"undo"' in m['content'] and 'sp_' in m['content'])
assert json.loads(commit['content'])['moved'] is True
push = next(m for m in round_msgs(seeds['git-flow']) if m['role'] == 'tool' and 'pushed' in m['content'])
assert json.loads(push['content'])['undo'] == ''
# the approval round still ends by asking once
rounds = warm_start([view_file, replace_text], dirs=[SEEDS_DIR])
denied = [m for m in rounds if m['role'] == 'tool' and m['content'].startswith('Denied by human operator')]
assert len(denied) == 1 and 'Reason given: no answer after 300s' in denied[0]['content']
final = rounds[rounds.index(denied[0]) + 1]
assert final['role'] == 'assistant' and final['content'].count('?') == 1 and 'nothing changed' in final['content']
assert rounds[-1] is final
# equal rank: library rounds (listed first) precede a seed; a same-model round wins the tie
def copy_of(r, name, model=None):
    return {'meta': {**r['meta'], 'name': name, 'model': model}, 'history': [{'role': 'user', 'content': [{'type': 'text', 'text': name}]}] + r['history'][1:]}
users = lambda ms: [m['content'] for m in ms if m['role'] == 'user']
q = users(round_msgs(seeds['search-choice']))[0]
with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    (Path(d)/'mine.json').write_text(json.dumps(copy_of(seeds['search-choice'], 'mine')))
    (Path(d)/'theirs.json').write_text(json.dumps(copy_of(seeds['search-choice'], 'theirs', 'm1')))
    test_eq(users(warm_start(ALL, dirs=[d, SEEDS_DIR], limit=4))[1:], ['mine', q, 'theirs'])
    test_eq(users(warm_start(ALL, model='m1', dirs=[d, SEEDS_DIR], limit=4))[1:], ['theirs', 'mine', q])
```

[`fit_rounds`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/core.html#fit_rounds)
does the selection for
[`warm_start`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/core.html#warm_start),
and also returns every accepted round it left out with the reason: a
tool that is not offered, a call that no longer binds to the offered
signature, or the `limit`. A warm-start screen can show those reasons to
a person, who can then act on them.

``` python
used, skipped = fit_rounds([search_code, grep, ls, view_file], dirs=[SEEDS_DIR], limit=10)
test_eq([r['meta']['name'] for r in used], ['search-choice'])
why = {r['meta']['name']: w for r, w in skipped}
test_eq(sorted(why), ['approval-refused', 'delegation', 'fossick-github', 'git-flow', 'memory-key', 'notebook-edit'])
test_eq(why['approval-refused'], 'tool replace_text is not offered here')
test_eq(why['git-flow'], 'tool git_status is not offered here')
used, skipped = fit_rounds({'view_file': view_file, 'replace_text': old_replace}, dirs=[SEEDS_DIR])   # the old dialect, offered under the real name
assert used == [] and dict((r['meta']['name'], w) for r, w in skipped)['approval-refused'].startswith('replace_text(path, edits) does not match this signature: ')
assert 'edits' in dict((r['meta']['name'], w) for r, w in skipped)['approval-refused']
used, skipped = fit_rounds(ALL, dirs=[SEEDS_DIR], limit=1)
test_eq([r['meta']['name'] for r in used], ['git-flow'])
test_eq({w for _, w in skipped}, {'over the limit of 1'}) and test_eq(len(skipped), 6)
test_eq([r['meta']['name'] for r, _ in skipped][:2], ['search-choice', 'notebook-edit'])   # skipped rounds keep the ranking too
assert fit_rounds(dirs=[SEEDS_DIR], limit=7)[1] == []   # no tools offered, room for every seed: nothing is skipped
assert warm_start(ALL, dirs=[SEEDS_DIR], limit=3) == [m for r in fit_rounds(ALL, dirs=[SEEDS_DIR], limit=3)[0] for m in round_msgs(r)]
```

[`register_completion`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/core.html#register_completion)
records a completion receipt: a new id stamped with the package version
and `ROUND_REVISION`.
[`completion_valid`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/core.html#completion_valid)
accepts the id only while both are unchanged, so a receipt from an older
round fails.

``` python
import tempfile
state = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())/'completions.json'
cid = register_completion(state); print(cid)
assert completion_valid(cid, state)
old = json.loads(state.read_text()); print(old)
old[cid]['version'] = 'old:0'
state.write_text(json.dumps(old))
assert not completion_valid(cid, state)
```

### main

``` python
def main(
    history:str='/home/runner/.config/ramabana/agent-history.jsonl', # Ramabana history path
    session:str=None, # optional session id
):
```

*Score the tool routes in a Ramabana history and print them as JSON.*

`dhrona` prints the assessment of a history as JSON. When the history
file is missing it exits with a one-line message.

``` python
from fastcore.test import expect_fail
with expect_fail(SystemExit, 'No history at'): main(history='/nonexistent/agent-history.jsonl')
```
